resale_co.name: Certificate of Continued Occupancy (CCO), now called Inspection Prior to Sale (IPS) on Township pages
resale_co.issued_by: Township of Mahwah Building Department (Construction Code Official)
resale_co.lead_time: The code says CCOs are issued or denied within 10 days of filing the application. The code also requires the CCO before the property is listed.
resale_co.valid_for: One year from the date of issuance, provided there is no material change in the physical status of the premises
requirements: Required for one- and two-family dwellings before the property is listed, and on transfer of title (homes with 3 or more units are exempt)
Visual inspection only (per the Inspection Prior to Sale form) by the Construction Code Official, who may call in subcode officials, the Water Department and the Department of Health
Check with the Health Department before applying that there are no septic system, cesspool or well tank issues
Inspection covers items such as pools, electric fixtures and wiring, plumbing fixtures and water heaters, heating and ventilation, the building exterior and other hazards
Any additions or construction done without permits must have permit fees paid before the CCO is issued
Separate smoke/CO certificate from Fire Prevention (not part of the CCO inspection)
Exempt transfers include deed corrections, transfers between spouses, parent and child or grandparent and grandchild, estate distributions, new construction and quitclaim deeds to quiet title
resale_co.how_to_apply: Fill in the Township's Inspection Prior to Sale form (owner, block and lot, realtor, phone, email) and return it with the $175 fee (check, e-check or charge) to the Building Department (Department of Inspections), 475 Corporate Drive, Mahwah, 201-529-5757. Check with the Health Department first that there are no septic, cesspool or well tank issues. The inspection is visual only.

Any questions or concerns about the CCO should be directed towards the building department and the Construction Official.
A certificate of continued occupancy shall be required in the following occurrences:

resale_co.notes: What changed: the Township now calls the sale inspection an "Inspection Prior to Sale" (IPS). The Fire Prevention page sentence now reads "instituted an inspection Prior to Sale (IPS)" instead of "instituted a CCO inspection", and still says CCO questions go to the Building Department. The Construction Office menu now links an Inspection Prior to Sale form (DocumentCenter 9597, named CCO-4-Inspection-Prior-to-Sale, Date Printed 7/27/2026): visual inspection only, Fee $175, payable by check, e-check or charge. This is the CCO form that was missing last time. The program itself and its $175 fee look unchanged. The rules come from Code 10-10 (Ord. No. 2065, added 8-4-2025): one- and two-family homes need the certificate before listing and on transfer of title, it is issued or denied within 10 days, is valid for one year, and costs $175 (also in the fee schedule, ecode360.com/34810206: "Certificate of Continued Occupancy - CCO Residential - Selling a Home $175"). ecode360 blocked fetches this check, so the code quotes are carried over from the October 4, 2026 read and were not re-read; no newer amendment showed in search results. If the CCO is denied, the Construction Code Official may allow the transfer if the buyer certifies in writing that violations will be corrected and an escrow is set up. The Township's Certificate of Occupancy page still says no CCO is required for a tenant rental; that is about rentals only.

requirements: Smoke detector on each level including basements (not attics or crawl spaces), and smoke and CO alarm outside each separate sleeping area within 10 feet of bedrooms
Homes built before January 1, 1977 may use 10-year lithium sealed battery smoke detectors; homes built on or after that date need hardwired detectors as originally required

The Township asks that hardwired detectors with removable batteries and detectors older than 10 years be replaced with hardwired 10-year sealed battery backup units; CO detectors replaced with 10-year sealed battery units
Low voltage monitored fire alarm systems must stay monitored and a copy of the alarm report must be included with the affidavit
Signed affidavit (Application and Certification) returned with the fee before the inspection
Portable fire extinguisher no longer required as of February 15, 2025 (the packet's form title still lists it)

authorities.name: Township of Mahwah Fire Prevention Bureau (Department of Fire Prevention)
authorities.lead_time: Contact the office or stop in to schedule once the application and affidavit are complete. If the change of occupant does not happen within 6 months, a new application is needed.

fees.label: Certificate of Smoke Alarm and Carbon Monoxide Alarm Compliance
fees.quote: A fee of $90 shall accompany the application.

authorities.how_to_apply: Download the Mahwah Fire Prevention Smoke Inspection Packet (or pick one up at the Building Department), complete the application and affidavit, and return it with $90 cash or check payable to "Township of Mahwah" to Fire Prevention, 475 Corporate Drive. Then call or stop in to schedule the inspection.
authorities.contact_title: Fire Official (Fire Inspectors Ed Garza and Nick Kovacs, ext. 290)

If the change of occupant does not occur within 6 months, a new application shall be required.

fire_cert.notes: The Township's Fire Prevention Bureau issues the smoke/CO certificate for a flat $90 (same in Code 12-1.8g); no tiered late fee is published. The Fire Prevention page says the portable fire extinguisher requirement was removed as of February 15, 2025, though the packet's form title still names it. The Fire Prevention page's packet links now point to DocumentCenter/View/9559, which returned not found on November 3, 2026; the packet at DocumentCenter/View/9113 (marked Updated 20-Oct-2025) still opens and is cited. The NJ DCA LEA registry lists Mahwah as a municipal (M) enforcing agency and the state fire directory (survey 7/22/2026) lists Fire Official Michael R Roe.

other_items.label: Tax search notice
other_items.detail: Tax searches and added assessment searches from the Tax Collector carry a notice that a CCO is required for a sale.

other_items.label: Unpermitted work
other_items.detail: If the CCO inspection finds additions or construction done without permits, the permit fees must be paid before the CCO is issued.

other_items.label: Water Department and Health inspection
other_items.detail: The CCO inspection may include the Water Department and the Department of Health.

other_items.label: Health Department check (septic, cesspool, well)
other_items.detail: The Inspection Prior to Sale form asks sellers to check with the Health Department that there are no septic system, cesspool or well tank issues before applying.
